Count the tail. Of all the gaps chance produced, what fraction reached as far as the one you actually saw?  That fraction is the **p-value**: the chance of data at least this extreme *if the no-effect story were true*.  Small p-value → the no-effect story explains your data badly.

How small is small enough? By convention, **p < 0.05** — a result that chance would produce less than 1 time in 20 gets called *statistically significant*.  That 5% is a custom, not a discovery. It buys you a mistake rate: even when nothing is going on, about 1 study in 20 will clear the bar by luck alone.
